mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes S 280 or S 420 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M112 engine for the S 280 costs £2,500-£3,800 supply-only; a rebuilt M113 V8 for the S 420 costs £3,200-£4,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity - V8 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of harmonic balancer failure on a Mercedes S 280?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unusual noises from the passenger side of the engine bay, vibration, or visible cracks in the rubber of the harmonic balancer are the classic warning signs on the M112 engine. If you notice any wobble from the main crank pulley, do not drive the vehicle.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes S 280 or S 420 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the M112 V6 and the M113 V8 are among Mercedes' most robust engines. The M113 is widely regarded as one of the most reliable German V8 engines ever built, capable of exceeding 300,000 miles with diligent maintenance. However, age-related issues like oil leaks, harmonic balancer failure, and ignition system wear are common and should be addressed proactively.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes S 280 and S 420 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M112 and M113 engines routinely reach 200,000+ miles before major work is needed. One owner reported an M113 engine exceeding 340,000 miles (500,000 km) with regular maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes S 280 or S 420 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the S Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M112 costs £2,500-£3,800 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£10,000 vehicle. The S 420's higher specification makes replacement even more justifiable for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes S 280 or S 420 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M112 V6 requires approximately 7.5 litres; the M113 V8 requires approximately 8.0 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 280/420 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The S 280 and S 420 launched with the W220 generation in 1998 as the entry-level V6 and mid-range V8 petrol flagships of Mercedes' luxury saloon range. The S 280 was powered by the M112 2.8-litre V6 producing 204hp, while the S 420 used the M113 4.3-litre V8 with 279hp. Both engines featured SOHC design with three valves per cylinder and timing chain drive, representing the pinnacle of Mercedes naturally aspirated engineering before the modern era of forced induction and direct injection. Production continued until 2005 when the W221 generation replaced the W220.

milestones.description: Minor ECU revisions to both engines for improved emissions
End of W220 production; replaced by W221 generation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz S Class 280 and 420 petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M112 harmonic balancer failure to M113 oil leaks and ignition system issues.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz S Class 280/420 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The S 280's M112 V6 and the S 420's M113 V8 are among Mercedes' most robust naturally aspirated petrol engines - renowned for their durability and longevity. However, with age and mileage, both have well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. The M112 is prone to harmonic balancer failure and oil leaks, while the M113 suffers from oil leaks, ignition system issues, and sensor failures. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M112 Harmonic Balancer Failure - The S 280's Signature Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M112's harmonic balancer (crankshaft pulley) has a bonded rubber layer that deteriorates with age, heat cycling, and exposure to oil and contaminants. This can cause the outer ring to separate at speed, potentially leading to catastrophic engine damage. This is the signature failure of the M112 engine family.

problems.h4: M112/M113 Oil Leaks - The V6 and V8's Age-Related Issue
problems.rootCause: Valve cover gaskets harden with age, causing oil to leak onto the exhaust manifold or into spark plug wells. Oil consumption and leaks from valve guide seals are also common. Approximately 30% of M113 owners report oil leaks as the most common issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, clean oil seepage
repairOptions.longevity: If oil leaks are minor and localised

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the M112 and M113 are common with age but not usually urgent unless they are heavy. Valve cover gasket replacement at a specialist is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. Use only OEM Mercedes-Benz gaskets - aftermarket seals are too thin and will leak.

problems.h4: M113 Ignition System & Sensor Failures - The S 420's Driveability Issues
problems.rootCause: The M113 V8 can suffer from ignition system failures causing engine misfires, reported by approximately 20% of owners. The crankshaft position sensor is known to fail, which can cause the car not to start or to stall. Mass Airflow (MAF) sensor failures and throttle body issues are also common.

problems.rootCause: The M112's variable intake manifold flaps can stick or seize, causing increased fuel consumption and loss of low-speed torque. Broken switchover linkages at the front of the intake manifold are also common.
